# CHALLENGER'S ANSWER — THE RECORD'S READING

**The reading I press:** In the King James Version the child Jesus has a named father among men, Joseph, and is of his body by seed according to the flesh. [L4]

## LINK C1 — THE SEED IS OUT OF A MAN'S BODY, ACCORDING TO THE FLESH

**Premise.** The promise requires seed proceeding out of a man's bowels and loins, and the New Testament says that seed is David's according to the flesh. [L4]

[L1] 2 Samuel 7:12 — "And when thy days be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom."
[L2] Standing in this verse: *zera* (H2233 — "seed; figuratively, fruit, plant, sowing-time, posterity") behind "thy seed."
[L3] Psalms 132:11 — "The LORD hath sworn in truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne."
[L3] 1 Kings 8:19 — "Nevertheless thou shalt not build the house; but thy son that shall come forth out of thy loins, he shall build the house unto my name."

[L1] Romans 1:3 — "Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;"
[L2] Standing in this verse: *sperma* (G4690 — seed) behind "seed."
[L3] Acts 2:30 — "Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne;"
[L3] 2 Timothy 2:8 — "Remember that Jesus Christ of the seed of David was raised from the dead according to my gospel:"
[L3] Hebrews 7:14 — "For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood."

**Chain.** [L1] 2 Samuel 7:12 states the seed proceeds out of bowels; [L2] *zera* stands there as seed/posterity; [L3] Psalms 132:11 and 1 Kings 8:19 state fruit of body and son out of loins. [L1] Romans 1:3 states Christ made of the seed of David according to the flesh; [L2] *sperma* stands there; [L3] Acts 2:30 states fruit of loins according to the flesh. Precept upon precept: real seed out of a man's body, according to the flesh, evident. A house register or a name taken by law does not show seed out of loins. [L4]

## LINK C2 — THE FATHER IS NAMED IN FOUR REGISTERS, AND THE RECKONING IS BY THE FATHER'S HOUSE

# Challenger, Round 2: the taking into the house, the throne of his father David, and the seed out of the loins

The defender has withdrawn Genesis 24:16 as footing for *ʿalmâh*, withdrawn Genesis 3:15, and narrowed D4. Two new inferences now carry the keystone D5:
- the conception falls before any knowing (D1, as now argued);
- the house of David is carried by name and record (D5, through Deuteronomy 25:6).

I answer each press of [CR2] with the rows, then close.

## 1. "Before they came together": Matthew narrates the coming together as the taking into the house

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L1]** Matthew 1:24: "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife."

**[L2]** *Paralambanō* (G3880) means "to receive near, i.e. associate with oneself (in any familiar or intimate act or relation)." It is the verb of Matthew 1:20, "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife," and of 1:24, "took unto him his wife."

**[L3]** The defender's own witness, Deuteronomy 22:24, calls the betrothed damsel "his neighbour's wife." Luke 2:5 has "Mary his espoused wife, being great with child."

**[L4]** Matthew's next narrated joining of the pair after 1:18 is the taking of 1:24. That is the verb the angel commands, "receive near, associate with oneself" [L2]. Two points follow:
- "Before they came together" dates the finding before the taking into Joseph's house [L1].
- The law calls the betrothed a "wife" from the espousal (Deuteronomy 22:24), and Luke still writes "his espoused wife" (Luke 2:5) [L3].

The defender's first horn makes the knowing of one's espoused wife into the coming together of 1:18. Matthew sets that coming together at the taking of 1:24. The second horn, Matthew 1:25 "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son," covers the time after the taking, and my link says the same.

So the canon's order, "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived" (Genesis 4:1), falls between the espousal and the finding. Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal. It fits the link.

## 2. "In those days ... with haste" (Luke 1:39)

**[L1]** Luke 1:39: "And Mary arose in those days, and went into the hill country with haste."

**[L2]** *Mnēsteuō* (G3423), "to betroth: espouse," stands in Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David."

**[L3]** Luke 1:56: "And Mary abode with her about three months, and returned to her own house." Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb."

**[L4]** "In those days" gives a span of days, with the conception future to the angel's word (Luke 1:31) [L1, L3]. Through that span Mary was "espoused" to Joseph of the house of David [L2]; she was a wife in law. Elisabeth's "blessed [is] the fruit of thy womb" (Luke 1:42) at Mary's arrival fits a conception within those days of the espousal. It fits the link. The defender's "No coming together lies between announcement and conception" equates knowing with the taking. Matthew 1:24 gives the taking as its own later act.

## 3. Luke 1:35's "therefore," and the throne promise applied to Christ

**[L1]** Luke 1:32: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."

**[L2]** *Kaleō* (G2564, "to call") stands in Luke 1:32 ("shall be called the Son of the Highest") and in 1:35 ("shall be called the Son of God"). It is the same calling in both verses.

**[L3]** Acts 2:30: "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."

**[L3]** 2 Samuel 7:12, 14: "thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels ... I will be his father, and he shall be my son."

**[L4]** The dio kai ("therefore") in v.35 connects back to v.32, not forward to biological divine paternity. The title is first given at 1:32 with "the throne of his father David," before Mary asks "How shall this be" in 1:34. Verse 35 repeats the calling [L2].

The defender says Solomon's case differs because "David's bowels are named in the same promise." Acts 2:30 applies that same bowels-and-loins half of the promise to Christ by name: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ" [L3]. For Christ, as for Solomon, the title and the loins stand in one promise.

The verbs of 1:35 are those of Acts 1:8, "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you," said of the apostles' power, and of Luke 9:34, "a cloud ... overshadowed them." They fit the setting apart of "that holy thing," beside the father in the flesh.

## 4. John 1:13 and Matthew 1:20

**[L1]** John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."

**[L3]** John 1:12: "But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name." John 3:6: "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit."

**[L2]** *Gennaō* (G1080): "figuratively, to regenerate."

**[L4]** John 1:13 is said of "as many as received him" (John 1:12). These are men born of the flesh of their own fathers, now born "of God" [L1, L3]. Birth "of God" stands beside a flesh birth in the same persons, as John 3:6 sets the two births side by side.

So *ek* with the Spirit in Matthew 1:20 fits the row that names, in one breath, "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" (margin: "conceived: Gr. begotten").

## 5. Matthew 1:19: the fear the angel answers

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife."

**[L2]** *Phobeō* (G5399): "to frighten, i.e. (passively) to be alarmed."

**[L3]** Matthew 1:19: "being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example."

**[L4]** The angel answers Joseph's alarm about taking her, and calls her "thy wife" [L1, L2]. Matthew 1:19 gives the two grounds of his intent: he was just, and he would not expose her before others [L3]. Both grounds concern her standing before the people. The finding "before they came together" (Matthew 1:18), that is, before the taking, is exactly what others would see. Joseph's intent to spare her that exposure fits a husband who is the father.

## 6. Deuteronomy 25:6 and Hebrews 7: the name, and the loins

**[L1]** Deuteronomy 25:6: "the firstborn which she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother [which is] dead."

**[L2]** *Shem* (H8034): "an appellation, as a mark or memorial of individuality."

**[L3]** Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." Hebrews 7:5: "though they come out of the loins of Abraham."

**[L4]** Deuteronomy 25:6 carries a name, a memorial [L1, L2]. Romans 1:3 and Acts 2:30 carry seed and loins "according to the flesh" [L3]. Hebrews 7 itself says how a tribe comes out: "out of the loins" (7:5), "in the loins of his father" (7:10). So the "evident" of Hebrews 7:14 stands in a chapter where descent is of the loins.

On "loins names the forefather": Matthew 1:2 shows the path from forefather to son, "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob." Levi was in Abraham's loins through each father's begetting. David's loins reach the child through the fathers to "Jacob begat Joseph" (Matthew 1:16), and to Joseph, "of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4). It fits the link.

## 7. Luke 2:48-50

**[L1]** Luke 2:27: "the parents brought in the child Jesus." Luke 2:41: "his parents went to Jerusalem."

**[L3]** 2 Samuel 7:14: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son."

**[L4]** Luke the narrator writes "the parents" and "his parents" [L1]. Mary writes nothing; she speaks "thy father and I." The child's "my Father's business" (Luke 2:49) stands beside these as God's fatherhood stood beside David's for David's son [L3]. That the parents "understood not" (Luke 2:50) is about the saying. Luke 2:41 still names them "his parents."

## CLOSE OF THE CHALLENGE

The defender's keystone, D5, now rests on two moves.
- It sets the knowing of a wife at the taking of 1:24, though Matthew narrates the taking as its own act after the finding (Matthew 1:18, 24).
- It carries the house of David by name alone, while Romans 1:3, Acts 2:30 and Hebrews 7:5, 10 carry it by seed and loins "according to the flesh."

The promise "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ" (Acts 2:30) is applied to Christ. The man of the house of David in the conception rows is Joseph, "thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20). The canon's means is "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived" (Genesis 4:1).

Christ had a biological father: Joseph, who knew Mary his wife within the espousal, of whose loins the seed of David came "according to the flesh."
